messages:
Jordan_Acme: Hey team — customer (Acme Mobile app) reports repeated mid-stream disconnects on SSE. Happens for users on T-Mobile and some MVNOs. App logs: "connection closed by peer" after ~80KB of chunks. Request-id: rq_8b7f2c. Seen across multiple regions.
Mia_support: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste server logs + a minimal repro? Is this HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 from the client?
Jordan_Acme: Client uses XHR SSE (HTTP/1.1). Quick repro steps I used:
```bash
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-small"
```
It starts streaming, then after a burst the connection resets. I captured edge log and snippet:
```
[edge] 2026-03-15T12:03:21Z conn=12345 client=18.220.12.33 rq=rq_8b7f2c: read: connection reset by peer
[edge] 2026-03-15T12:03:21Z upstream: POST /v1/stream -> 504? broken pipe
```
Jordan_Acme: Also saw a kernel tcpdump showing ICMP "fragmentation needed" on the path earlier in the trace.
Devon_engineering: Interesting — that smells like PMTU/MTU fragmentation issues. Many mobile carriers block ICMP type 3 code 4, so the sender never learns to lower MSS and large chunks get dropped mid-stream.
Raj_oncall: Can you share the pcap or at least tcpdump -vv output around the reset? Look for "frag needed" or ICMP unreachable. Also check if client is behind a carrier NAT that rewrites seq numbers.
Jordan_Acme: Pcap extract: 
```
IP 10.1.2.3 > 34.56.78.9: Fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu 1400) icmp_seq 42
TCP 34.56.78.9: Flags [P.] seq 345678:346900 ack 12345 win 4128 
... then 1s later RST from client IP
```
Mia_support: Good find. That matches customer environment (carrier MTU ~1400). Our default SSE flush chunk occasionally emits >1500B frames when generating, so intermediate devices drop them.
Devon_engineering: Server-side mitigations we can try: (1) enable MSS clamping on the edge  (2) reduce SSE chunk flush size (buffered flush to 1KB) (3) enable chunked transfer with smaller buffers. I can push a flag to the edge to cap outgoing segment size for that customer.
proxy-bot: Action logged: created ticket EDGE-2987 for MSS clamping rule for cid=acme-client, scheduled patch to edge pool deploy at 2026-03-16T01:00Z.
Jordan_Acme: Before the patch, any quick customer workaround? They are not able to change carrier.
Devon_engineering: Easiest immediate workaround: client can set EventSource polyfill to re-open with smaller Accept or throttle reads, but realistically server change is faster. Also recommend switching to chunked keepalive smaller than MTU.
Jordan_Acme: I applied a small server-side experiment: limited SSE flush to 900 bytes and retried with same client. Repro failed — no disconnect after 3 long requests.
Raj_oncall: Nice. Can you paste a short before/after log?
Jordan_Acme: Before: 
```
[edge] SEND chunk size=1742 id=rq_8b7f2c
[edge] client reset after 0.9s
```
After: 
```
[edge] SEND chunk size=896 id=rq_9c8f4d
[edge] stream closed gracefully by client after completion
```
Mia_support: Great root cause: PMTU/DF + large SSE chunks => middlebox drops => client RST. Workaround confirmed. We'll coordinate permanent edge patch. Please ask customer to test on a few more devices.
billing-bot: Note: partial chunks delivered are billed proportional to tokens delivered; retries don't double-bill if client reconnects and resumes (we bill based on actual tokens returned). If they think billing looks doubled, open a billing ticket and attach rq IDs.
Jordan_Acme: Will do. Also adding their device logs. Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:.
Devon_engineering: I'll schedule the MSS clamp rollout and add a config flag to reduce default SSE chunk size for mobile-tiered routes. Follow-up in EDGE-2987.
Raj_oncall: Marking thread as triaged. If anyone sees any new RST spikes after the deploy ping here.
Jordan_Acme: Closing from my side for now, will reopen if customer sees new disconnects. Thanks everyone.
